name: Boac Cathedral
description: Perched on a hilltop fortress in Mataas na Bayan since 1792, the Immaculate Conception Cathedral Parish is a coral-stone landmark and declared Important Cultural Property.
howToGetThere: Take a jeepney from Balanacan Port to Boac town proper (~35 min), then walk uphill behind Boac Plaza or ride a tricycle to the parish gate.
bestTime: Early morning daylight for stonework photos, Sunday Mass, or Holy Week observances.

name: Tres Reyes Islands
description: A trio of forested limestone islets—Gaspar, Melchor, and Baltazar—rising off Gasan's southwest coast, known for quiet white coves and reef snorkeling.
howToGetThere: Ride a tricycle south from Gasan Centro to Brgy. Pinggan dock, then charter a 30–45 min outrigger bangka to Gaspar Island (~PHP 1,000–1,500; TODO: verify current port boat rates).
bestTime: November to May mornings for calm seas; avoid southwest monsoon swells from June to October.

name: Mt. Malindig
description: Marinduque's highest summit (~1,157 m), a mossy stratovolcano and wildlife sanctuary offering dramatic ridge views across southern Luzon and Sibuyan waters.
howToGetThere: Travel to Buenavista Centro and take a tricycle to the Brgy. Sihi trailhead to register and hire a mandatory local guide for the ~4-hour summit climb (TODO: verify current barangay guide fee).
bestTime: Pre-dawn dry-season hikes (November to May); trails often close during heavy monsoon rains.

name: Poctoy White Beach
description: A sweeping kilometer-long curve of fine cream-white coral sand fringed by coconut palms, facing crystal blue waters and the silhouette of Mt. Malindig.
howToGetThere: Ride a van or bus from Balanacan Port or Boac to Torrijos (~1.5–2 hours), then hop a 5-minute tricycle east to Brgy. Poctoy shoreline.
bestTime: Dry-season weekdays and golden sunrise mornings from December through May.

name: Maniwaya Island
description: Laid-back northeast outer island lined with long pale beaches, calm reef shallows, and seaside homestays serving as the launch point to Palad Sandbar.
howToGetThere: Take a van to Santa Cruz Centro (~1.5 hours from Boac), tricycle 10–15 min to Buyabod Port (not Balanacan Port), and board a 30–45 min boat (no ATMs on the island; TODO: confirm daily public boat schedule).
bestTime: March to May sunny summer months; arrive morning to catch public bangka departures.

name: Palad Sandbar
description: An ephemeral crescent of bright white sand that rises from turquoise coral flats northeast of Maniwaya Island only when tides drop. TODO: verify exact low-tide bar GPS on site.
howToGetThere: Join a ~20–30 min boat hop from Maniwaya Island or charter a bangka from Buyabod Port in Santa Cruz (~PHP 1,500–4,000 + barangay fee; bring shade and water, zero shelter on the bar).
bestTime: Morning low tide windows between March and May (check daily tide tables before departure).

name: Malbog Sulfuric Spring
description: Geothermal mineral pools (~36–40°C) fed by volcanic springs at Mt. Malindig's southern foothills, tucked beneath breezy rain-tree canopy.
howToGetThere: Take a coastal jeepney to Buenavista town proper and ride a tricycle inland to Brgy. Malbog (~PHP 25–50 entry; remove silver jewelry before soaking).
bestTime: Cool weekday mornings between December and February (typically ~6 AM–5 PM; TODO: confirm current resort hours).

name: Bathala Caves
description: An eight-chamber limestone karst complex set in wooded hills of Sitio Bathala, famous for high vaulted galleries and rock formations. TODO: verify exact cave trailhead GPS in Brgy. Ipil.
howToGetThere: Ride a tricycle ~10 km north from Santa Cruz Centro to Brgy. Ipil, register at the barangay hall, and hire a required local guide (~PHP 50 entry + ~PHP 300 guide; bring sturdy shoes and headlamp).
bestTime: Dry-season mornings from November to May; lower caverns can turn slick during heavy rain.

name: Moriones Festival
description: Marinduque's signature Holy Week Lenten street drama where penitents in hand-carved wooden Roman helmets re-enact the legend of Longinus across Boac, Mogpog (origin town), Gasan, and Santa Cruz. Event pin anchored at Boac Plaza.
howToGetThere: Fly or ferry via Balanacan Port to Boac or Mogpog town plazas (~30–40 min by jeepney); processions wind through town centers island-wide.
bestTime: Holy Week annually from Palm Sunday to Easter Sunday (TODO: confirm exact March/April dates for your trip).
